Solution The base of D is also the region’s projection R on the xy-plane. The boundary of R is the circle x2 + (y - 1)2 = 1. Its polar coordinate equation is
The region is sketched in Figure 15.46.
Cartesian: x2 + (y − 1)2 = 1 Polar: r = 2 sin u
We find the limits of integration, starting with the z-limits. A line M through a typical point (r, u) in R parallel to the z-axis enters D at z = 0 and leaves at z = x2 + y2 = r2.
Next we find the r-limits of integration. A ray L through (r, u) from the origin enters R at r = 0 and leaves at r = 2 sin u.
